observationsNotFindings: fx13Proves is not carried, where live v9's FX-13 proves is 'DISCLOSURE'. I examined whether this is the residue of the pattern I charged at FX-5 and FX-6 and concluded it is not, on the test I have applied all session: does the omission make a statement false or drop content that survives nowhere else? Neither. FX-5's and FX-8's proves fields carry substantive qualifications absent from their intents - FX-5's split label, FX-8's 'INVALID if only the first half is run' - so losing them lost real content. FX-13's proves is the single classification word DISCLOSURE, and every limitation this class carries is already in the fully-quoted intent and restated at the subject's identityValues field. Recorded because the two accepted successors in this family, FX-6 v2 and FX-8 v2, both carry a proves field, so a later consistency pass may want it here; not charged, because nothing is lost by its absence.

This is the fourth FX corpus I have reviewed in this stretch and the first whose v1 quotes its v9 intent whole. FX-5 v1 dropped 62%, FX-6 v1 altered 66% with a terminal-punctuation substitution, FX-8 v1 dropped a 161-character tail; all three lost the class's honesty statement, and all three needed a v2. FX-13 v1 does not need one. FX-10, FX-11 and FX-12 still have subjects on disk with no Claude 2 verdict and have not been checked for this defect.

The seven states carry no platform, race or boundary axis. Live v9's FX-13 intent names none, unlike FX-4 whose intent says 'on both platforms', so declining to cross any second axis is correct rather than an omission.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no SHOULD-FIX. I ran the truncation check first and by string equality, because three consecutive corpora in this family failed it this session and needed a v2. It does not recur: fx13Intent is 492 characters and equals live v9 exactly, including the limitation sentence routing Run/operation identity values to DR-006 / ID-DEP-P12. The seven closed-set tokens are v9's permissionVocabulary list in the same order, and v9 states that vocabulary is closed at seven, so the one-chain-per-token coverage is exactly right with nothing invented or dropped. All four byte slots on all seven states are NOT-AUTHORED and identity values are NOT-ASSERTED - and I swept for value shapes rather than trusting the labels, finding zero UUIDs, zero run-*/op-* identifiers and zero RequestId/ExecutionId literals, with bare integers limited to 0, 1, 03 and 26. ID-DEP-P12 is real: v9's L-8 transition says the identities of Run/operation are not minted there and ride DR-006's parked recipes. One thing recorded and deliberately not charged: fx13Proves is absent where v9's proves is 'DISCLOSURE'. Unlike FX-5 and FX-8, whose proves fields carried qualifications missing from their intents, this one is a bare classification word and every limitation is already in the fully-quoted intent, so nothing is lost - though the two accepted successors in this family do carry proves, so a consistency pass may want it. FX-10, FX-11 and FX-12 remain unreviewed and unchecked for the truncation defect. 15 attacks run, 15 refuted.
